summary: Isaac's Harbour light on Holly Point, first lit in 1874, was replaced by a combined lighthouse and dwelling in 1928 or 1929; it has been privately owned and closed since 2018.

access.note: Private property. A gate on the access road is about 600 m from the lighthouse; permission is reportedly needed (LighthouseFriends). Visible from the end of the access road and from NS-316.

events.note: First put in operation 9 November 1874 as a fixed red light in a square wooden building 20 ft high (LighthouseFriends quoting the 1874 Department of Marine report)
Built by J. T. Sinclair under contract for $870 (LighthouseFriends)
Changed on 1 May 1877 to two fixed white lights, one in the lantern and one from a bay window 20 ft lower
Ira L. Giffin appointed keeper, 28 April 1894, at $265 a year
Hand fog horn established at Isaac harbour, to be sounded when vessels' fog signals are heard

Two fixed white lights replaced by one occulting white light from a 4th-order dioptric apparatus, in the year ended 31 March 1910; new octagonal iron lantern painted red. NSLPS dates the 4th-order occulting lens to 1922.
SS John Irwin foundered off Isaacs harbour on 25 July 1911; total loss, twelve lives lost. The return does not mention the light.
Present combined lighthouse and dwelling built to replace the original. Parks Canada and LighthouseFriends give 1928; the Lighthouse Directory and NSLPS give 1929.
Last keeper, Ernest B. Davidson, retires; the light is automated and he stays on as caretaker
Coast Guard declares the lighthouse surplus (January 1990) and plans to replace it with a fibreglass tower
Recognized as a federal heritage building, 13 December 1990, after a Federal Heritage Building Review Office score of 54
Discontinued in spring 2009 (LighthouseFriends; Lighthouse Directory says inactive since 2009). Parks Canada gives 2008.
Recognized as a heritage lighthouse; LighthouseFriends gives May 2018, the Lighthouse Directory June 2018, and the Parks Canada backgrounder is dated 4 June 2018
Sold to a private owner, who began restoring the interior. Owner not named here.

corrections.why: The standing tower is the building that replaced the 1874 light. Parks Canada and LighthouseFriends give 1928; the Lighthouse Directory and NSLPS give 1929. The 1874 date belongs to the first light, not to the standing structure. A human should choose between 1928 and 1929.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Parks Canada and LighthouseFriends give 1928 for the present lighthouse; the Lighthouse Directory and NSLPS give 1929. The story gives both dates and says the sources differ.
Parks Canada says the original was destroyed by fire; LighthouseFriends says the old lighthouse was demolished once the new one was built. The story reports both.
Parks Canada gives 2008; LighthouseFriends and the Lighthouse Directory give 2009 (spring 2009 and 'inactive since 2009'). The story gives both.

LighthouseFriends gives May 2018 for the heritage recognition; the Lighthouse Directory gives June 2018; the Parks Canada backgrounder is dated 4 June 2018. The story uses the backgrounder date for the announcement only.

The 1910 Chief Engineer's report and LighthouseFriends both date the change to one occulting white light to 1910. NSLPS lists a 4th-order dioptric lens with group occulting white under 1922. The story follows the 1910 report and does not explain the 1922 entry, which is left for a human check.

notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-27: all 60 quotes were found on the first run. Record change: focal_height_m 25.0 removed from facts because no source gives a focal height for the present light (the 1874 light was 80 ft, about 24.4 m, and that is in the story only). Story changes: the 1874 light's 80 ft and the 1877 lens distances are now metres first; the 1877 keeper's living space is about 1.1 m2 (12 sq ft); the 1910 change is dated to the year ended 31 March 1910 and the NSLPS 1922 date is now stated as a disagreement; Bigsby's landing is 'near the lighthouse' in LighthouseFriends' narrative (not the report text); the 1909 list is described as a statement of light-keepers, and the 1900 'Holly Point, Isaac's Harbour' entry is in that statement; the Webb/first-settler sentence now reports LighthouseFriends' two statements without merging them; 'initially' restored in the Parks Canada line; the hedge 'could be very oppressive' restored; the Giffin/Griffin spelling is stated as LighthouseFriends' roster (Giffin) against its narrative (Griffin); the 1900 foghorn and hand foghorn wording dated to the fiscal year ended 30 June 1900; the 1900 $25 extra is worded as LighthouseFriends gives it. Page checks: the 1900 fog horn passage is scan p. 64 printed p. 49 (checked against corpus.py page); the 1910 lights entry is scan p. 92 printed p. 92; the 1912 casualty return is scan p. 237 printed p. 230 (the footnote's scan p. 237 matches the URL n237); the 1900 statement p. 129 is scan p. 226 (checked). The Griffin row (1909, scan p. 167, printed p. 160) is matched by position in one OCR line that carries name, date and salary but not the station: the page image was NOT viewed by the checker, so a human must confirm the station on that row before the 1894 appointment is attributed to Isaac's Harbour. The 'Ira L. Griffin' OCR line also splits 'April'. The Parks Canada backgrounder date 2018-06-04 is the page's metadata date; LighthouseFriends' references give June 4, 2018. Earlier note follows. Dates for the present building differ: 1928 (Parks Canada, LighthouseFriends) and 1929 (Lighthouse Directory, NSLPS). The record's built 1874 is wrong for the standing tower. Parks Canada says the original was destroyed by fire, LighthouseFriends says it was demolished; neither is checked against a newspaper, since the Chronicling America search for 'Isaac's Harbour' with 'lighthouse' (1874 to 1930) returned nothing. Deactivation is 2008 in Parks Canada and 2009 in LighthouseFriends and the Lighthouse Directory. Keepers: the 1874 report is not in the corpus (the corpus starts in 1900); its wording is taken from LighthouseFriends' quotation and marked as such. The 1909 list's OCR splits 'April' as 'A pril' and the quote is copied as OCR'd; the matching is by position in a row (name, date, salary), and a human should check scan p.167 (printed p.160). Giffin is spelled Griffin in the 1909 list and Giffin in LighthouseFriends; the story uses Giffin and says so. Sinclair, MacMillan and Davidson come only from the LighthouseFriends roster; the Department's 1915-1924 lists did not give keeper names for this station in the OCR. J. MacMillan has no end date. Davidson's stint (1938 to 1966) is named only as a published roster names it. The 1910 report says 'Isaac Harbour, South Coast', and the 1900 report's hand foghorn list says 'Isaac harbour'; both are this station. A 1905 entry headed 'Fisherman harbour' with a contractor of Isaac harbour is a different light and is not used. A 1906 hydrographic note about a schooner off Isaac harbour is unclear in OCR and is not used. The owner of the lighthouse since 2018 is a private person, not named. The Canadian Register entry 4805 returned only its title and the Parks Canada DFHD page is script-driven, so the register's own statement was not read. The Coast Guard List of Lights was not checked for a current status.
